requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was written with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, daemon-reload'd, then enabled --now. systemctl status shows it loaded/enabled/active with the worker script and its sleep child as the running processes, matching the pre-existing binary confirmed against the prepare baseline (same script content observed).

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account (not root)
requirements.summary: inventorysvc was confirmed absent beforehand, then created as a system account (uid/gid 999, no home, nologin shell) via sudo useradd. The unit specifies User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps directly shows the running worker and sleep processes owned by inventorysvc/inventorysvc, not root.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e4e401d2... with service enabled/active was captured, matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' was issued and acknowledged (connection subsequently dropped), then a poll cycle showed connection-refused followed by a new boot_id fb6d915e..., matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot exactly. Post-reboot, systemctl shows inventory-worker enabled/active with a new PID, and ps confirms the worker and its sleep child are owned by inventorysvc, demonstrating full recovery through an actual, bounded disruption.

overall_summary: The task's material requirements are all satisfied with direct evidence: the pre-existing os-comparison-worker binary is run as a systemd unit named inventory-worker under a newly created, unprivileged inventorysvc system account, confirmed by process ownership both before and after a genuine reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and cross-checks cleanly against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (e4e401d2... before, fb6d915e... after), with the service shown enabled/active and correctly owned in both states.
limitations: The reboot's transient /tmp/reboot.log output was not directly inspected, though its absence post-reboot is consistent with normal tmpfs/boot cleanup rather than residue.
No long-running observation window after recovery was captured beyond the immediate post-reboot check, so longer-term stability under the new boot is inferred rather than directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tight and purposeful: discovery, one failed useradd attempt without sudo (cmd-363672ce2a3546fc, no state change since it errored before creating the account) immediately corrected with sudo (cmd-56d4c3406c2c43e6), unit creation, enable/start, verification, then the required reboot cycle for restart evidence. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the temp-file diff (old boot systemd-private dirs replaced by new-boot ones) is an expected artifact of the reboot itself, not executor residue. The nohup-redirected /tmp/reboot.log from the shutdown command left no trace in the post-executor temp-file listing.
